questions.question_text: Which one of the following observations is correct for the features of logarithm function to any base $b>1$ ?
questions.question_html: Which one of the following observations is correct for the features of logarithm function to any base $b>1$ ?

options.label: A
options.text: The domain of the logarithm function is $R$ , the set of real numbers.
options.html: The domain of the logarithm function is $R$ , the set of real numbers.

options.label: B
options.text: The range of the logarithm function is $R^{+}$ , the set of all positive real numbers.
options.html: The range of the logarithm function is $R^{+}$ , the set of all positive real numbers.

options.label: C
options.text: The point $(1,0)$ is always on the graph of the logarithm function.
options.html: The point $(1,0)$ is always on the graph of the logarithm function.

options.label: D
options.text: The graph of the logarithm function is decreasing as we move from left to right.
options.html: The graph of the logarithm function is decreasing as we move from left to right.

questions.explanation_text: $\because$ Domain $\in R^{+}$ and range $\in R$ and graph of the logarithm function is increasing. So, point $(1,0)$ is always on the graph of logarithm function.

questions.question_html: The value of $e^{log_{10}tan1^{\circ}+log_{10}tan2^{\circ}+log_{10}tan3^{\circ}+\dots+log_{10}tan89^{\circ}}$ is
questions.explanation_text: We know that $tan\theta tan(90^{\circ}-\theta)=tan\theta \cdot cot\theta=1$ $tan1^{\circ}tan89^{\circ}=tan2^{\circ}tan88^{\circ}=tan3^{\circ}tan87^{\circ}=tan44^{\circ}tan46^{\circ}=1$ So, $log_{10}tan1^{\circ}+log_{10}tan2^{\circ}\dotslog_{10}tan89^{\circ}$ $=(log_{10}tan1^{\circ}+log_{10}tan89^{\circ})+(log_{10}tan2^{\circ}+log_{10}tan88^{\circ})+\dots+(log_{10}tan44^{\circ}+log_{10}tan46^{\circ})+log_{10}tan45^{\circ}$ $=log_{10}(tan1^{\circ}+tan89^{\circ})+log_{10}(tan2^{\circ}+tan88^{\circ})+\dots+log_{10}(tan44^{\circ}+tan46^{\circ})+log_{10}tan45^{\circ}=log_{10}1+\dots+log_{10}1+log_{10}1$ $=0$ Thus, $e^{elog_{10}tan1^{\circ}+log_{10}tan2^{\circ}+\dots+log_{10}tan89^{\circ})}$ $=e^{0}=1$
questions.explanation_html:
We know that

$tan\theta tan(90^{\circ}-\theta)=tan\theta \cdot cot\theta=1$

$tan1^{\circ}tan89^{\circ}=tan2^{\circ}tan88^{\circ}=tan3^{\circ}tan87^{\circ}=tan44^{\circ}tan46^{\circ}=1$

So, $log_{10}tan1^{\circ}+log_{10}tan2^{\circ}\dotslog_{10}tan89^{\circ}$

$=(log_{10}tan1^{\circ}+log_{10}tan89^{\circ})+(log_{10}tan2^{\circ}+log_{10}tan88^{\circ})+\dots+(log_{10}tan44^{\circ}+log_{10}tan46^{\circ})+log_{10}tan45^{\circ}$

$=log_{10}(tan1^{\circ}+tan89^{\circ})+log_{10}(tan2^{\circ}+tan88^{\circ})+\dots+log_{10}(tan44^{\circ}+tan46^{\circ})+log_{10}tan45^{\circ}=log_{10}1+\dots+log_{10}1+log_{10}1$

$=0$

Thus, $e^{elog_{10}tan1^{\circ}+log_{10}tan2^{\circ}+\dots+log_{10}tan89^{\circ})}$

$=e^{0}=1$
